text:
jamal: Heads up - CI is red on main after the toolchain roll, looks like both Bazel and CMake jobs failing. Putting a bisect in flight. Error snippets below.
ci-bot: [auto] Build failed: //...:all (linux-x86_64, macos)
alex: Can you paste the failing output? is it link error or compile?
jamal: macos clang compile error: undefined reference to 'pthread_atfork' in third_party/foo
jamal: Bazel output snippet:
```
ERROR: /workspace/third_party/foo/BUILD:12:1: Linking of rule '//third_party/foo:libfoo' failed: clang failed: error executing command
Undefined symbols for architecture x86_64:
  "_pthread_atfork", referenced from:
      _foo_init in libfoo.a(foo.o)
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture x86_64
```
maria: Hmm that looks like a libpthread mismatch; toolchain roll bumped libc/toolchain flags? also seeing cflags changed: -D_GNU_SOURCE removed in the new image
alex: we saw similar earlier — maybe the gcc -> clang default changed and -pthread isn't implied anymore.
jamal: CMake job fails too: linking fails with "cannot find -lstdc++_nonshared" on macos, weird stdlib symlink issue.
ci-bot: Rerun queued: relaunching macos-build shard 7 (requested by jamal)
maria: @jamal can you start a binary-search on the toolchain images? I can help with the CMake side and quick link-workarounds.
jamal: starting bisect across toolchain image tags now (rolling from image v2026.02 -> v2026.05). Will post findings.
alex: If bisect points to image change, capture /usr/lib/libpthread and clang --version output from both images so we know what changed. I can run a container diff next.
jamal: running lightweight container diff:
```
# old image (v2026.02)
clang --version: Apple clang version 14.0.6
/usr/lib/libpthread.dylib -> present (symlink)
CFLAGS: -D_GNU_SOURCE -O2
# new image (v2026.05)
clang --version: Apple clang version 15.0.2
/usr/lib/libpthread.dylib -> missing (replaced by libSystem?)
CFLAGS: -O2
```
maria: Ok that explains it. New image removed an implicit flag or changed runtime layout on macos. Quick mitigation: explicitly link -pthread in third_party/foo CMakeLists.
jamal: added tiny patch to force -pthread when building libfoo, opened PR and triggered CI.
devex-bot: PR #4821 created by jamal: fix(macos): add -pthread to third_party/foo link flags 
alex: Nice. If that makes CI green we should plan a proper fix in the toolchain images (or update our buildpack).
maria: FYI linux CI rerun green — failure is macos-specific.
jamal: macos rerun with PR patch passed on shard 7. Marking bisect result: regression introduced in image v2026.05, but immediate fix is the explicit -pthread link.
alex: Can you add a minimal test that links a tiny pthread program to catch this in future? Put it in ci/smoke/macos-link to guard against regressions.
maria: adding test in follow-up commit. Also logging an infra ticket to chat with infra/toolchain team to revert or document change.
jamal: created INF-453: macos toolchain image removed implicit pthread link; tracked to toolchain image changes.
ci-bot: Build passed: macos-shard-7 (rerun)
jamal: closing the bisect and leaving the PR until toolchain image is fixed upstream. Thanks for the quick help everyone. :thumbsup:
alex: will schedule a 15m sync tomorrow to align on release and backport plan.
maria: thanks, will prepare the repro steps and diffs for the toolchain team.
